_rule: An IndexMeasure (elohim_epr_rea::index) and a Manifest EPR; it deserializes straight into the protocol type, CIDs spelled as strings, and is compiled into elohim-storage (include_str!) and validated at boot. The storage peer's lexical fold over its own content projection: one unit per content row (unit_id = content.id). Each unit folds as a 'head' section (title, a blank line, description), the body (content_body) chunked by _chunk_rule — markdown bodies (content_format markdown) split at headings, every other body into line windows — and a 'tags' section (the row's tags joined). It ranks by FTS5 bm25() over those chunks; it pins no model and never runs an embedder. The fingerprint is the content's own CID (blob_cid when the row names one, else the raw CID of content_body); a retitle or retag re-folds too, because the stored stat is the raw CID of the head and tags text. A run folds at most foldLag.limit changed units, in one transaction, and writes its attestation beside the store. The store is <storage_dir>/index/<measure-cid>/fold.sqlite: derived, rebuilt on corruption, never a migration, never synced. The measure's method CID is IndexMeasure::cid() over the typed value; the underscore keys are not part of it.
_chunk_rule_note: The same _chunk_rule object the recall measures declare (.epr-meta/elohim/algorithms/recall-semantic-index.json), so chunkRule is the same CID: one chunker, two folds. It is re-hashed at boot and must address to chunkRule.
_reach: A ceiling at self: the fold is a machine-local projection that never leaves the peer. Reach is gated per reader, per candidate, when an answer is assembled — never by leaving rows out of the fold.
_retention: Retention has no fold-count period, so 'demote at the next fold' is declared as a zero delay: a content row that is gone, or whose fingerprint moved, has its chunks demoted by the first fold that observes it, never deleted.
